title: gad ask Invocation Record
description: Captures a single invocation of `gad ask`, whether in pure-ask (readonly) or agent (action-taking) mode. Logged to .planning/.gad-log/<date>.jsonl with tool='gad ask'. Drives tool-use DPO mining via result.actions_taken and permission_check_result emissions. Sibling to tool_use_preference.schema.json.

ts.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the invocation was created (before inference begins).

operator_id.description: Operator who initiated this invocation. For direct CLI calls this is the authenticated user. For agent-dispatched calls this is still the human operator (agent_id carries the agent attribution).

agent_id.description: ID of the agent that dispatched this invocation. Null when the operator fired it directly from their CLI. Set when a subagent or worker called `gad ask` on behalf of the operator.

parent_agent_id.description: ID of the parent agent if this invocation is nested inside an agentic loop. Null for top-level invocations. Allows attribution chains to be reconstructed for DPO mining.

mode.description: Execution mode. 'ask' = pure semantic lookup, no actions taken. 'agent' = soul plans and executes tool actions subject to the permissions tier. CLI flag: --mode=ask|agent. Default: ask.

permissions.description: Permission tier governing what actions the agent may take. Only evaluated when mode=agent. CLI flag: --permissions=readonly|safe|dangerous. Default: readonly. See gad_ask_permission_tiers.schema.json for tier definitions.

query.description: The operator's natural-language query or instruction. In mode=ask this is interpreted as a question. In mode=agent this may be an imperative ('deploy modal vllm endpoint', 'reclaim stale claims').

soul_route.description: Soul routing resolution at invocation time. Resolved from soul_routes.toml. Snapshot stored here so replay is stable even if routes.toml changes later.

soul_id.description: Name of the soul selected. Example: 'kael', 'gilgamesh'.

base_model_id.description: HuggingFace model ID or API model slug. Example: 'Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct', 'claude-haiku-4-5'.

adapter_stack.description: Ordered list of LoRA/PEFT adapter paths applied on top of base_model_id. May be empty if using a fine-tuned checkpoint directly.

context_built.description: Context window assembly report. Populated after retrieval, before inference.

sources.description: Ordered list of context sources injected into the prompt.

ref.description: File path, dataset ID, or content hash identifying the source. Example: '.planning/DECISIONS.xml', 'retain-banks/kael/v3'.

token_count.description: Tokens contributed by this source to the final context window.

total_tokens.description: Total tokens in the assembled context window.

truncated_at_token_budget.description: True if one or more sources were trimmed to fit within the token budget.

rag_index_version.description: Version hash or build timestamp of the repo embedding index used for retrieval. Null if retrieval was skipped or index does not exist yet.

result.description: Inference result. Null when status=pending or status=running. Populated on completion or failure.

answer_text.description: Natural-language answer returned by the soul. Present in mode=ask. May also be present in mode=agent as a preamble before or summary after actions.

structured_outputs.description: Machine-readable outputs extracted from the answer. Schema is query-dependent. Example: { 'handoffs': [...] } for a stale-claims query.

cost_usd.description: Total cost of this invocation in USD. Includes retrieval + inference. Excludes cost of actions taken (logged separately via spend ledger).

tokens_in.description: Input tokens consumed by the inference call.

tokens_out.description: Output tokens emitted by the inference call.

latency_ms.description: Wall-clock time from invocation start to result delivery in milliseconds.

citations.description: Source references cited by the soul in its answer. Drives citation DPO signal.

snippet.description: Short quoted excerpt from the cited source. Optional — include when the answer paraphrases rather than directly quotes.

actions_taken.description: Ordered list of tool actions executed by the agent. Populated only in mode=agent. Each entry is a candidate for tool_use_preference DPO mining — the action is the 'chosen' branch; what a worse model would have done (file-foraging, manual shell, etc.) is the 'rejected' branch derived from the query type.

tool.description: Tool or CLI command invoked. Example: 'Bash', 'gad handoffs reclaim', 'modal deploy'.

inputs.description: Key inputs to the tool. Abbreviated — enough to reconstruct intent and drive DPO pairing.

permission_tier_at_execution.description: Permission tier active at the moment this action was evaluated. Inherited from invocation.permissions unless overridden by an explicit-authorize gate.

output_summary.description: One-line summary of the action result. Example: '3 claims reclaimed, 0 skipped'.

cost_cap_usd.description: Per-invocation cost cap in USD. If inference + action cost would exceed this, the invocation is aborted with status=aborted_cost_cap. Null = no cap (use gad-config.toml default). CLI flag: --cost-cap.

session_id.description: GAD session ID under which this invocation was made. Allows session-level cost aggregation.

status.description: Lifecycle state of this invocation. 'aborted_permission_violation' = agent attempted an action whose tool_kind exceeds the declared permissions tier; invocation halted and a permission_check_result record was emitted.

examples.query: where does worker-loop call rotation in vendor/get-anything-done

result.answer_text: worker-loop.cjs calls rotation at line 214 via `rotateRuntime(ctx)` imported from runtime-rotation-policy.cjs. The call site is inside the `tick()` function after a worker heartbeat timeout is detected.

examples.query: what's pending in claimed/ — reclaim anything stale

result.answer_text: Found 2 stale claims (>4h, no heartbeat). Ran dry-run — confirmed reclaimable. Awaiting operator confirmation before committing reclaim.
Deploying modal_app/serve_vllm.py. This action has real-world side effects (spend, public endpoint). Proceeding under permissions=dangerous with operator authorization confirmed.

actions_taken.output_summary: deployed kael-sft-serve, endpoint live at modal.run
